judged_text: Service construction now unconditionally POSTs to login.salesforce.com for a fresh access token and writes the credential row on every SalesforceCalendarService instantiation, replacing jsforce's lazy refresh-on-expiry flow. Every booking create/update and availability check on a Salesforce-connected calendar gains a Salesforce token-endpoint round-trip plus a DB write even when the stored token is valid, and a Salesforce outage or token-endpoint rate limit now fails every one of those operations at construction time instead of only expired-token paths.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the service now performs an immediate `fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)` using the stored `refresh_token`, then updates the DB via `prisma.credential.update(...)` before constructing/returning the `jsforce.Connection`. This happens during service setup (not gated by any `isExpired`/expiry check in the shown diff), so simply instantiating/initializing the Salesforce service will incur a token-endpoint round-trip and a credential row write even if the existing access token is still valid. That is a concrete, diff-grounded performance/availability concern and shifts failures (Salesforce outage/rate limiting) to construction time rather than only on refresh-needed paths, but it’s not provably a functional correctness defect from the diff alone.
